source.title: Brain endothelial gap junction coupling enables rapid vasodilation propagation during neurovascular coupling

limitations: Adult male mice; Online Methods state two to three months, but Supplementary Table 2 reports mean ages of 14.8 weeks for C57BL/6 and 17.0 weeks for knockout laser-Doppler cohorts. No exact universal age range is admitted. No randomization, blinding, prospective sample-size calculation or exclusions were reported.

Kcnj2 deletion uses constitutive Tek-Cre, not adult-induced capillary-only deletion. Isolated cEC currents and control smooth-muscle currents support endothelial attribution but do not exclude developmental effects or establish restriction to one vascular segment. Identical listed genotyping primer pairs require verification before protocol reproduction.

CaPA is an isolated, pressurized preparation with sealed capillary ends, not normal flowing blood. Diameter, upstream smooth-muscle voltage and in vivo flux come from separate recordings. Membrane-potential recordings use wortmannin to suppress movement. Estimated conduction speed is inferred from distance and onset, not voltage measured along every endothelial cell.

Whisker responses persist after endothelial Kcnj2 deletion. Surface barium has a broader target range and leaves residual perfusion responses. The potassium source during neural activity and the complete intercellular route remain unresolved; potassium ejection bypasses the physiological release step.

Raw recordings and custom MATLAB LFP software have not been obtained or reproduced. The reporting checklist and main text do not provide a resolved access route. No numerical edge weights, universal minimal carrier counts or independently validated full pathway are assigned.

Aortic electrical measurements, retinal tracer spread and awake cortical responses are distinct preparations. Cerebral endothelial voltage is not recorded along the full route. Gap junctions can carry small molecules as well as current; residual vascular responses and alternative routes prevent identification of a unique complete neural-to-vascular mechanism.

contexts.finding: Selected birth-labeled neurons acquire neuronal morphology and electrophysiological responses. Input integration is supported in this preparation; unbiased generation rates, mature output transmission and memory necessity are not tested.
limitations: Female C57BL/6 mice were four to five weeks old at housing allocation and received virus one week later. Birth labeling therefore starts at approximately five to six weeks, not uniformly in fully mature adults. Electrophysiology was four to eight weeks after injection and used runners only.

Retroviral GFP labels a selected dividing-cell population. Variable infection, neuronal GFP downregulation and faint cells prevent absolute neurogenesis-rate estimation. BrdU incorporation is a separate DNA-labeling assay; a 48-hour count is not a count of mature functional neurons.

Of 58 recorded GFP-positive cells, 13 from 13 mice had neuronal physiology; 45 were nonexcitable and not all individually identified. The 13/58 fraction is a selected recording yield, not an unbiased neuronal differentiation probability. Unlabeled comparison neurons were not birthdated.

Sample sizes vary by assay and parameter. Table 3 compares up to 13 labeled neurons and 27 unlabeled neurons from 23 mice; cell nesting is not a fully reconstructed animal-level analysis. Randomized housing allocation, blinding and a prospective sample-size calculation are not reported in the reviewed Methods.

Spontaneous postsynaptic responses were seen in six labeled neurons, and perforant-path-evoked responses in four. Selective transmitter blockade is not supplied for every input. The paired-pulse example does not establish a universal sign rule, and afferent input is not direct proof of output transmission to CA3.

Table 3 nonsignificant comparisons are not equivalence tests. The membrane time constant differs, and capacitance is calculated from time constant/input resistance rather than measured as a direct morphological quantity.

The four-week and four-month morphology samples contain different cells. Eight cells are used per age for most measures, with five for four-month spine density; their animal distribution is not resolved. This is not longitudinal tracking of the same dendrite.

Running and standard housing have separate BrdU samples of five and four mice. Housing is a multicomponent exposure, not a selective learning manipulation. Normal adult neurogenesis does not thereby require training or tissue injury.

Main experimental text, Methods, Figures 1-5 captions and Tables 1-3 were read in the PMC author manuscript; Figures 3-5 were visually inspected. Raw recordings, animal-identified data and the LabVIEW acquisition code were not obtained or replayed.

No behavioral memory test or selective newborn-neuron ablation is performed here. Cell birth labeling, neuronal markers, synaptic morphology, input responses and cognitive necessity are distinct claims.

limitations: Cross-sectional postmortem hippocampal samples compare young adults (YA), healthy agers (HA), preclinical intermediate pathology (PCI), Alzheimer disease (AD) and SuperAgers (SA). There is no randomized diagnosis, in vivo birthdating, lineage follow-up, electrophysiology or neurogenesis intervention.

The main text reports 38 participants, including eight HA, whereas both cohort-table sheets and the abundance workbook contain 39 sample IDs, including nine HA. Identical demographic/pathology fields occur for some different IDs; this does not prove duplicate donors. The donor/sample manifest and independence remain unresolved.

Rare cell labels depend on quality filtering, reference-assisted annotation, marker expression and model-based trajectory inference. RNA-velocity latent time is not elapsed lineage time. A UMAP embedding is not measured physical tissue geometry.

The abundance analysis uses per-sample counts and library-size normalization, not absolute whole-hippocampus numbers or neuron birth rates. Published log-fold changes and adjusted P values are retained as reported comparisons; edgeR analysis and sequencing data have not been rerun.

SuperAgers come from Northwestern, while the other groups come from the University of Washington. Tissue source, individual variability and clinical selection can confound group comparisons. The Methods and main text differ in their reference age wording for SuperAger memory criteria; a uniform clinical manifest is required.

Reviewed material comprises main pages 1264-1267, Discussion on page 1272, Methods covering donors, nuclei isolation, sequencing and admitted analyses, Figure 2, Extended Data Figures 1 and 4 and all three reporting-summary pages. Main pages 1268-1271 and the remaining extended-data analyses were not fully reviewed.

Original Supplementary Tables 1 and 8 and the table legends were read; selected numeric cells and the complete sample/count census are checked locally. Other supplementary table contents were not audited. GEO GSE268609 is named by the paper, but its sample manifest and raw data were not obtained; no study-specific executable code was replayed.

The SA immature-cell comparison is significant against HA and AD, but not against YA or PCI at the table adjusted-P threshold of 0.05. These distinct contrasts neither prove no difference nor establish that generating neurons preserves memory.

The study measures morphology and output transmission, not behavior. Proposed recruitment of existing spines is a cross-sectional interpretation, not an observed minimal construction rule or proof of memory necessity.

The manipulation reduces Bax-dependent cell death in the Nestin stem/progenitor lineage; it is not a selective increase in birth rate or a dentate-newborn-neuron-only intervention. Olfactory-bulb survival also changes. Reporter recombination is a proxy, and altered cell properties or other lineage effects remain alternative mediators.

Main Figure 2c alternates the order of contexts across days, whereas the discrimination Methods describe training context A followed one hour later by similar context B. The exact per-animal schedule requires reconciliation. The nine-day ratio analysis reports treatment P=0.023; its day F/degree-of-freedom/P combination also needs correction. Handling of a zero sum of freezing scores is unspecified.

Contextual freezing discrimination is a behavioral proxy for pattern separation, not a direct measurement of DG neural population codes or general memory improvement. Supplementary protocol variants have treatment P=0.38 and P=0.06 despite interactions or day-specific differences; they cannot be pooled as uniformly positive main effects.

Supplementary Figure 14 reports an overall discrimination-ratio treatment P=0.1 and interaction P=0.3. Late within-group differences are not a between-group necessity test. Its day-five F(1,14)=4.34/P=0.04 pair needs reconciliation; no replacement biological P value is calculated here.

The paper explicitly leaves functional significance untested. No electrical recording, identified synaptic output, behavioral mediation or selective birth-cell perturbation establishes functional integration in these human samples. Findings in mouse integration experiments cannot supply those missing human measurements.

Whole hippocampi were analyzed; the investigators could not separately radiocarbon-date hippocampal subdivisions. Dentate localization and absolute cell-number scaling rely on other histological and stereological studies. The approximately 700 neurons per day in each hippocampus and 0.004% of dentate neurons per day are model-dependent estimates, not directly counted daily births.

No human electrical, identified synaptic-output or selective behavioral assay is performed. Similar estimated rates across species do not supply human functional integration or a birth-to-cognition mechanism. Histology, isotope dating, molecular markers and rodent interventions remain distinct evidence.

No electrical, synaptic-output, learning or memory assay was performed. A possible cognitive role, stable-memory benefit or recovery mechanism remains untested. Labeling in this study does not require an injury or learning manipulation and does not validate the source card's necessary incoming assertions, weights or minimum carrier counts.

Specific rat learning protocols alter retained birth labels; a separate macaque study supplies age-limited neuronal colabels. Neither establishes a universal learning prerequisite or a selective newborn-neuron requirement for memory.

Rakic (1985) and Eckenhoff and Rakic (1988) propose that stable neurons preserve learned information. Their autoradiographic nulls contain no matched memory test and appear to share specimens. This proposed stability mechanism and later renewal-benefit hypotheses are not adjudicated by histology alone.

Pattern separation, temporal context and memory resolution remain nonexclusive interpretations. Behavioral discrimination, population-code decorrelation and temporal association require different measurements; review schematics cannot choose among them.

Its six milestones are type 1, type 2a, type 2b, type 3, early postmitotic and late postmitotic states. They describe developmental features rather than six disjoint populations.
